en.title: Minimum and Maximum Endpoint Cost of a Partition into a Fixed Number of Segments
en.description:
Split the array into exactly k non-empty contiguous segments; each segment costs its first element plus its last element, and a single-element segment counts that element twice. Output the minimum and maximum total cost.

The standard I/O, examples, and judging were written independently by CSWork; conventions marked as this site's are not presented as original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n k (1≤k≤n≤200000), and the second line contains n positive integers (1..10⁹).
en.output: Output the minimum total cost and the maximum total cost.
en.explanation: Example 1: the fixed cost of the first and last elements is 6, and the cut weights are 3, 5, 5, 7; the minimum takes 3 and 5 for 14, and the maximum takes 7 and 5 for 18. Example 2: both ends of the single-element segment are 7, for a cost of 14. Example 3: the array must be split into [1] and [2], for a cost of 2+4=6.
hints: The first and last elements always contribute; every other contribution is the sum of the two adjacent elements at a cut. Choose the k−1 smallest or largest adjacent sums.
